body: **2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the flight booker's select in the stand's tables and readings) — 0.2.0's cold-agent-bar chunk, this entry's direct precedent: it put `select#flight-type` on the stand (`ComboBox` named `Flight type`, options `ListBoxOption`s, exactly the chosen one `selected`) and pinned that a driver `click` on a flight-type option is refused `covered`. Why it matters: it is the origin of the `covered` refusals on a closed select's options that this chunk's wrong-call-by-cause counts must now read (contract/driver-click-refusals/covered), and it was a stand change that moved no engine crate. This chunk's boundary is the same: no verb, carrier or cause changes.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the served pages, their open gap, the lint's option overlap and the scrollbar's band) — recorded the six tasks `escher-session` serves (Cells and the load page among them, neither a `LeanTask`), with `unkeyed_actionable` empty on all six. It also recorded the trap that right after a `scroll`, a driver `click` inside the overlay scrollbar's band is a thumb drag and dispatches nothing until an `advance` passes the fade. Why it matters: the served pages are what a cold agent reaches over MCP, and the scrollbar band is a known way for an agent's call to go wrong that a wrong-call reading may meet.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (a `multiple` select's keys and row clicks) — under Kept: an option of a closed single select stays refused `covered`, on the founder's F8/F9. Why it matters: this is the founder's word behind the `covered` clause on a closed select's option, the refusal cause this chunk's verdict will count by cause.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (`optgroup`, its role, its name and its options; the driver on a `multiple` select) — `optgroup` became `Role::Group` and its options became the select's own options in tree order. A disabled group's rows read disabled through `option_disabled`, one rule shared by the readings and the form entries (decision/disabled-optgroup-one-rule, contract/single-select/optgroup-options). The `display: none` exception was widened to options under an `optgroup`. The driver's `type` on a `multiple` select focuses with no click and adds nothing to the driver's closed sets. Why it matters: these are the rows the select list's run leg rests on, and they set the precedent that driver behaviour on a select adds no verb or cause, which this chunk's boundary repeats.

**2026-10-20-select-by-id** — the select entered the tree. A select's option is excepted from `display: none` (it stays in the tree; `hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still exclude it). The option's chosen state reads `selected` with no `aria-selected`. A select's changed choice marks the changed set. Why it matters: this is the origin of the hidden-content exception rows (contract/accessibility-tree-hidden-content/display-none, decision/hidden-content-excluded, decision/hidden-content-excluded-from-a11y-tree, contract/accessibility-tree/hidden-and-inert-nodes) and of contract/accessibility-tree-states/select-option, which a cold agent's snapshot of the flight booker reads.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the select list as a scope entity) — added the Select list row: an engine overlay on every document, remote pages included, that a closed single select opens. Hit testing answers it first and it is painted after the root. SC 2.1.1, 2.4.3 and 1.4.3 are asserted in the harness, and the AT reading is `unrunnable-here`. Why it matters: decision/single-select-engine-overlay-list. The scope's v030-17 leg (a click on `select#flight-type` opens the list) runs against this row, and the CARRY on `wrong_calls` read by cause comes from this chunk's report.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (a click, the pointer and focus on an open list; an open list against `:open`, clips and `opacity`) — each click on a single select opens its list or closes one standing, and a row of an open list takes a click. Focus stays on the select. A driver `click` on an element under the list is refused `covered`. Under Kept: a closed select's option is still refused `covered` (F9). Why it matters: these are the two `covered` clauses (contract/driver-click-refusals/covered) that the scope says can move `wrong_calls`, unread until this chunk. A cold agent that clicks the select and then something under the list meets them.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (what the snapshot and an assistive technology read of an open list) — a select whose list is open is no closed select, and an open row's `bounds` is its painted row's, the diff naming `bounds`. No `expanded` node key exists (`NODE_FIELDS` thirteen then). The highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree, a stated limit seen only in a screenshot. Why it matters: contract/snapshot/select-list-rows, contract/snapshot/open-list-row-bounds, contract/snapshot/open-list-highlighted-row and absence/snapshot-list-open-state. A cold agent working the list from the snapshot cannot see the highlight or the open state, so wrong calls on the list may trace to these limits.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (a single select's `expanded` in the tree; a group's label painted as a header) — a single select reads no `aria-expanded` and writes `expanded` from its list's open state. An author's `open` or `aria-expanded` steers nothing, and the tree's focus stays on the select. An `optgroup` label is painted as a header that chooses nothing, heavier by weight on every build. Why it matters: decision/single-select-expanded-from-list, contract/accessibility-tree/single-select, contract/accessibility-tree/select-expanded and contract/select-open-list/optgroup-header are the readings the select-list capability shows a cold agent.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the changed set where a list stands) — a single select's list opening or closing marks the changed set, and so does a page scroll or wheel that closes a standing list. A highlight or wheel move inside the list marks nothing. Why it matters: decision/changed-set-marks, which the later 2026-11-13 row edit restates. It decides what a cold agent's acting-call diff shows when it opens or closes the list.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list's checks and the legs they run in; the driver's `type` on any select) — the list's keyboard and focus coverage is headless, with SC 2.1.1 and 2.4.3 asserted in both layout modes and the windowed list read and not run. `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted` and `stand_act_popup` run outside the a11y leg. The driver's `type` on any select focuses it with no click and closes any list. Why it matters: decision/select-list-coverage-headless and decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click. The list's existing headless witnesses stand beside the run, and this chunk's scope leaves the windowed list out.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (how an open list's labels leave) — an option's label and a group's `label` leave an open list only as painted pixels in a `screenshot` and the snapshot's `name`, with no log site. Ratified by the founder (F7, F1). Why it matters: decision/option-labels-leave-only-as-pixels. A live cold-agent run that opens the list carries those labels to the model provider through screenshots and snapshot names. The span or cause counts this chunk adds must not add a log site that holds them.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on `dioxus-native-dom` unconditionally, with no `[features]` table of its own, because its executor reads the snapshot. Both seven_guis binaries compile the tree override, snapshot, text and diff, and neither builds a platform adapter. Why it matters: decision/driver-requires-accessibility and decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility. Every MCP read the widened pipe asks for (`graph`, `actions`, `layout`) stands behind this feature edge in `escher-session`.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is worded on the presence reading the snapshot's `enabled` uses. The driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own. Rule: whatever detects `disabled` reads the snapshot's `enabled`. Why it matters: the refusal causes this chunk counts by closed word are this schema's causes, and `disabled` is one the stand's `flight-return-date` and CRUD controls produce.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — `Session::run` refuses a `click` or `type` as `disabled` where `enabled` reads `Some(false)`, as the first of its screen-level checks, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was. Why it matters: contract/driver-actions/disabled and contract/driver-refusal/disabled. A `disabled` refusal is one of the endings the verdict's new cause counts will read from the `command` span.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — the obs log format is restated as two record classes: one line per printed event, and one line per closed span of an admitted target (`span={name}`, the span's recorded fields, `message`/`time.busy`/`time.idle`), both behind the target allowlist. Why it matters: the pipe's `COUNTED` reads accepted `tool_call` span lines, and the cause counts need the `command` span's `cause` field in `server.log`. This is the record class those reads parse.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — the sink's second record class (one line per closed span) reads as ratified by the founder, 2026-10-09. Why it matters: the closed-span lines the cold-agent verdict counts, and from which it will read refusal causes, are a ratified format and no provisional one.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the sink prints only safe fields for `blitz*`/`accesskit_xplat`, redacts `text`, `value`, `html` and `attrs` for `escher_*` targets, and drops any other target's record whole, at every level. Why it matters: it decides which span fields reach `server.log` at `RUST_LOG=info`. Whether the `command` span's `cause` survives the scrub is the inferred precondition of the scope's cause counts, and the closed-word, no-text verdict rests on that redaction.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP tool result reads the snapshot model and nothing else: a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output and an acting call's result is its JSON line with the diff. The snapshot's text reaching an MCP client is the crossing the founder ratified 2026-10-10. Why it matters: contract/mcp-result/snapshot. The cold agent reads only these results, and the scope's F3 crossing question (graph and actions answers sent to the model provider) sits beside this ratified crossing.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts. An MCP `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output for a whole screen and the JSON line `{text, part, parts}` for a paged one, and `MASKED_VALUE` holds in every part. Why it matters: contract/mcp-result/snapshot in its current form, which is what a cold agent on Cells meets. The fake server in `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py` must answer in these shapes.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — a password typed through an MCP `type` reads `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, and the typed sentinel occurs 0 times, in both layout modes. The node keys' help and `differs` are readers that write closed words only. Why it matters: decision/password-value-masked, decision/password-never-revealed and contract/snapshot/password-value hold on the MCP carrier the cold agent uses. A widened task must not lead to a reading that reveals typed text.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — a password is painted as bullets in every frame and renderer. The driver's `screenshot` reads only the model's bounds and changes nothing: no focus move, `has_changes` false, the next diff empty. Why it matters: `screenshot` is one of the `COUNTED` verbs, and the masked paint is the guard on what a live run's screenshots carry to the model provider (decision/password-never-revealed).

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part: the contrast reading through the `lint` verb) — the visual lint's `contrast` reading is carried as the `lint` verb on every carrier. A finding is written as `id` · `defect` · `bounds` · `ratio` · `required`: ids, closed words and numbers only. The founder ratified this carriage. Why it matters: `lint` is one of the `COUNTED` verbs. Its answer shape and the stand's boot reading (no finding, per 2026-10-31-engine-debts' overlap fix) are what a cold agent's lint calls read.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the lint's closed-select overlap ended) — the lint stopped reading a closed select's options as overlapping. The flight booker at boot reads `[0, 0, 0, 0]`, and the stand reads no finding of any kind at boot. Why it matters: in 0.2.0's run the stand's one boot finding was that overlap. A 0.3.0 cold agent's `lint` calls now read a clean stand, a changed baseline next to 0.2.0's 66 calls.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the read-only UI graph reader `DioxusDocument::graph`; the «reacts to a click» snapshot field) — `DioxusDocument::graph` was added behind `accessibility`. It holds one node per snapshot node and carries ids, component, state and handler event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value. A graph read changes nothing. No served id holds `///`. `NodeState.clickable` was added (`NODE_FIELDS` 14). Why it matters: decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node, decision/ui-graph-carries-no-values and contract/node-id/reserved-separator. These are the answers the `graph` verb, now asked of the cold agent, carries to the model provider, and the scope names them in F3's crossing question.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (graph state registration and the bridge dispatch's write record) — apps register state through `use_graph_state` with authored `DeclaredWrite` declarations. Each signal write is recorded against the dispatch and reads `undeclared` or `unconfirmed`. Why it matters: these state names and flag words are the content of a `graph` answer the widened task asks for. The contract tests' fake server answers `{"nodes":[],"states":[]}` against this shape.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the one actionable rule and the check's listener leg; the actionable-node reader) — `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes` share one crate-private actionable rule (`Readings`: focusable, an interactive role, or exact current listeners other than `mounted`). `data-dioxus-id` serves event dispatch alone. `actionable_nodes` lists graph nodes with `id`, `owner` and `keyed`. Why it matters: decision/one-actionable-rule and contract/actionable-nodes/listing are the rule behind every node an `actions` call answers.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actions verb as a read-only reader) — `Session::actions` answers, for each actionable node and each verb that takes an id, the cause `check_target` would refuse it with, `stale` where no element resolves. It changes nothing (an open list stays open) and writes ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text, `MASKED_VALUE` or `NodeId`. On the stand the flight booker's options read `covered` until the list opens. The founder ratified the verb's crossing onto every carrier. Why it matters: decision/actions-verb-changes-nothing, contract/actions-answer/causes and contract/actions-answer/fields. An agent that reads `actions` first can avoid `covered` and `disabled` refusals, which bears directly on `wrong_calls`. Its answers are what F3's crossing question names.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actionable counts at boot and the Cells answer's bound) — `ACTIONABLE_AT_BOOT` pins Counter 2, Flight Booker 7, Timer 3, CRUD 11, Cells 678 and the load page 2. On Cells the unpaged `actions` answer is 106,088 bytes, a stated limit owned by residual `res-7cc5bi4k`. Why it matters: a cold agent asked to call `actions` on Cells gets an answer of about 106 KB. That bears on the live run's cost against 0.2.0's $0.8244 baseline and on what crosses to the model provider.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the keyed reading, provisional on the carriers) — the `keyed` field on the `actions` answer is the actionable-key check's wire form, true where the id holds no `/`. It was PROVISIONAL as the overseer's delegate call. Why it matters: decision/keyed-wire-form is a field of the answer the widened task asks for. Its later ratification is the next item.

**2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap** — `~ decision/keyed-wire-form`, state provisional → standing, on the founder's «Утвердить keyed (Рекомендую)». Why it matters: the `keyed` field a cold agent reads in `actions` answers is ratified, so no founder fork hangs on it in this chunk.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** (the ungated reached record on handle_event's path; handler_coverage, a further reader of the UI graph) — `record_reached` / `reached_handlers` are an ungated record on `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event`'s path: first-reached order, deduplicated by (id, event), and one `has_context` lookup per dispatch on every other document. `escher_driver::handler_coverage` reads the graph and answers ids, owner ids, event names and two counts only. Why it matters: contract/dioxus-document/reached-handlers, contract/dioxus-document/record-reached and contract/handler-coverage/answer. The scope names handler coverage (the `coverage` role, no MCP tool) as out of the cold agent's reach, with its own headless witness standing.

**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** (2. A11y Strategy) — `~ decision/changed-set-marks`: the rule gains «a scroll that closes a list included; … any other scroll». Why it matters: this is the current text of a picked row. A cold agent's `scroll` while the flight-type list is open closes it and marks the select in the diff.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — added `docs/capabilities.md`'s `## Accessibility reach` as a scope entity: tier 0, SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3, the AT reading unmeasured, the named limits. Its pin reads none of these claims, so a change is made by hand. Why it matters: the founder's F2 decides what this run's result may claim on `docs/capabilities.md`. Any edit there must leave the accessibility reach section consistent and stated by hand.

**2026-11-18-capability-statement** — `~ decision/capability-statement-reach-by-hand`, why: the capability statement's pin now reads only the a11y leg's file count among that section's claims. Why it matters: it is the previous chunk's change to the same document F2 touches (`docs/capabilities.md`). An edit there under F2 is held by that pin's leg-count read and by nothing else in the a11y section.

body: The UI graph read (graph verb) asked of the cold agent: read-only, one node per snapshot node, carrying no values; its answer's ids, owner ids, component and state names cross to the model provider in a live run.
The actions answer asked of the cold agent: the actions verb changes nothing; its fields and its cause words are what the agent reads and what a live run carries out.
The layout read asked of the cold agent, an instance verb on every carrier, counted like graph and actions where the run asks for it.

The single-choice select list opened by a click on the flight booker's select (an engine overlay list): the task asks the agent to open it; the snapshot's list rows are what it reads, and option labels leave an open list only as pixels.
The driver click refusal cause covered, including its clause on an option of a closed select: it can move wrong_calls, and the verdict now counts refusals by their closed cause word, no text.
The caused reading on an acting answer, asked only where a served stand step causes a panic, error or record.

Indirect, through the obs log the pipe reads: one line per closed span of an admitted target, with the target allowlist redacting text, value, html and attrs for escher's own targets; the cause counts read the command span's cause field from that log and add no field, span or log line.
No driver verb, carrier, argument, cause, session error, log field or span is added or changed; no listener, env read or secret; the pipe reads what the server already writes.

The capabilities a cold agent cannot reach are named out of the run's reach, each with its headless witness standing: handler coverage (its answer is the coverage role, no MCP tool), the headless select list coverage, a fixture state, exploration, a component alone, the seed, bundled fonts.
The verdict's wrong-call judgement: one named bar constant, its value the founder's, the contract tests pinning pass and fail at the bar's edge whatever the value.
The contract harness stays offline (shim and fake server), each new count, cause count, capability-unused reason and the widened task tested red before green; the pipe never fires in CI or a loop.

What a live run's answers carry out to the model provider (graph and actions answers not named by the earlier ratification; a password value is never revealed in any answer) is recorded as part of the founder's word to run live, not decided here.

Keyboard navigation contracts (range input keys, Cells grid, CRUD list, the select's closed-list and open-list keys, Tab order, keyboard activation): the agent's task uses the select by a click and no key behaviour changes.
Visual design and contrast rows (the lint's contrast finding, stand contrast, scrollbar thumbs, select list colours and motion): nothing painted or measured changes.
ARIA property reads, accessibility tree states, role mapping and accessible-name precedence: no accessibility tree reading changes; the pipe only asks for answers the server already gives.
The AccessKit platform adapter, the accessibility feature's defaults and the assistive-technology reach absence: no adapter, feature or assistive-technology witness is in this chunk.
Hidden and inert content, focusability and focus fixup rules: the chunk adds no element, attribute or focus behaviour.
UI graph state registration (use_graph_state, unconfirmed, undeclared) and the Dioxus reached-handler record: the chunk registers no state and records no handler.
Cognitive accessibility rows (invalid state not by colour or class alone, the shared tab-order table): no stand app or form changes.
The windowed select list and the MCP protocol's next revision: named by the scope as not this chunk.

**2026-10-06-cold-agent-run-pipe** — registered the cold-agent pipe (`scripts/cold-agent.sh {run <task> | status | cleanup | logs}`, exits 0 · 1 · 2 · 3, python3-`json` events, `verdict.json` `passed` only on positive evidence, `scripts/cold-agent.ps1` a pass-through, `target/cold-agent/` state area uploaded by no CI job, pinned by `test_cold_agent.py` in the `ci-scripts` leg); its client, outbound path and login a boundary widening. Origin of the CLI grammar, exit codes, state area and pass-through Windows entry this chunk extends without changing.

**2026-10-06-founder-rulings** — the cold-agent crossings (the `claude` client, the `claude -p` session, the model provider through the operator's own login, the spawned processes) ratified by the founder. Precedent: the provider crossing is the founder's to widen; F3 (the live run's word) and the new answers' carriage rest on it.

**2026-10-06-stand-test-contract** — registered the agent-run contract and `target/agent-run/`, local only and never uploaded, beside which the cold-agent state area sits (decision/run-state-areas-local-only, decision/agent-state-areas-local). Any new state file the widened verdict writes stays inside `target/cold-agent/` under this rule.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the one verb table `VERBS` and `Cause` closed at eight with fixed names; standing rule: a verb joins `VERBS`, never a second table. Cause-by-cause refusal counts in the verdict must use exactly these closed words.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — the `command` span (target `escher_driver`, INFO): `verb` and, on a refused call, `cause`; never an argument or screen content. The verdict's new cause counts read this span's `cause` field from `server.log` — the field exists by this entry, and a refused call records `verb` and `cause` only.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the sink admits only the engine and `escher_` prefix sets; an escher target prints every field not in `CONTENT_FIELDS`. Whether `cause` reaches `server.log` at `RUST_LOG=info` depends on this scrub rule (the scope's P3 read).

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — ratified the sink's closed-span line (one line per closed admitted span, its fields in recorded order). The pipe counts `tool_call` span lines and would count `command` span lines; this is the line shape it parses (contract/telemetry-line/span-close-line).

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — the session socket carries driver calls and answers (ids, names, masked values, snapshot text, diffs), ratified as a widening; `validate_session` and the CLI's endings. Base of decision/socket-carries-driver-calls; the boundary rule that a new carrier, exit or field widens, which this chunk must not trip.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the `escher-session mcp` role and the `tool_call` span with only `tool` and `ending` (accepted, refused, error), the parent of `command`; standing rule: no span field holds what a call supplied. The verdict's `wrong_calls` reads `refused`/`error` endings of this span; per-cause reading must go to the child `command` span, since `tool_call` carries no cause and no field may be added (scope boundary).

**2026-10-12-self-description** — the program's own fixed text (help, remedies, tool descriptions) rides the ratified carriers, ratified; text from a page, a call or a screen still widens. Bears on a widened stand prompt: the prompt is the pipe's, but what it causes the agent to carry is screen content.
**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — the `screenshot` verb and its in-band image on MCP; one of the three verbs `COUNTED` already counts (`screenshot_calls`) and requires for `capability-unused`.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** — `covered`'s second limit (a one-axis clip stops a hit at the whole padding box, so a showing element can read `covered`). A cause the per-cause wrong-call reading can count that is the engine's limit, not the agent's error.

**2026-10-15-cold-agent-test** (both entries) — moved the pipe onto the workspace's own `escher-session mcp` (MCP server `escher`, `--allowedTools mcp__escher`, `--model claude-opus-5-5`, `--max-budget-usd 3`, task `stand`, `STAND_PROMPT`), the server child at `RUST_LOG=info` writing `server.log` (never printed or copied), `counts_agree` against `tool_call` span lines, the replayed `check.json`, the judge stdlib python3 with no package; the provider row carrying the stand's screens, ratified («Один запуск, до $3», «JSON-проверка с повтором»). The pipe's whole present shape: decision/cold-agent-isolated-session, cold-agent-judge-stdlib-python, cold-agent-mcp-server-is-own, raw-run-output-never-printed, cold-agent-run-carries-stand-screen.

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** (Driver session and CLIs entry) — `time-unavailable` retired, causes closed at eight with `fonts-unavailable` the eighth; `advance` moves the clock on every session. The closed cause set the verdict's cause counts enumerate, and `advance` as a counted verb.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** — the recording directory named only by `--record`, created `0700`, kept checks owner-only and never logged (decision/recorded-session-checks, record-dir-launcher-named-private). The live server child records into `target/cold-agent/record`; the verdict's `recording-not-kept` reason rests on it.

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — each kept answer whole at rest; `Check::replay`. The verdict's passing-then-ablated replay of the agent's check depends on it; a check with `graph`/`actions`/`layout` steps replays their answers whole.
